acceptable_risks: RTD/GitHub canonical URLs 404 — definitionally unreachable until the repo and RTD project exist; resolves on push
Full ~100-test suite gates main rather than every PR — acceptable trade-off given runtime cost; merge-blocking subset still covers the critical jax-hlo path
Coverage gate enforced only on main — 79.7% headroom over 71% means PRs are unlikely to silently regress past the floor before main catches it
Subprocess-based LSP harness reports 0% line coverage in the parent — a measurement artifact, not a behavioral gap
README omits the version subcommand and jaxlint_rules/jaxlint_version MCP tools, and docs/lsp.md still says 0.4.0 — cosmetic doc drift, fixable in a 0.4.2 patch
Classifiers don't enumerate 3.11/3.12 explicitly — requires-python >=3.11 already constrains installs correctly; cosmetic for PyPI faceting
Missing [project.urls] — PyPI page will lack sidebar links until added; trivially fixed before or immediately after first publish

Add Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11 and :: 3.12 classifiers (and a Typing :: Typed line if py.typed ships)
Bump version to 0.4.2 in pyproject and docs/lsp.md and refresh README to mention the version subcommand and jaxlint_rules/jaxlint_version MCP tools
Create github.com/maraxen/jaxlint, push main, enable the Read the Docs project so the documented URLs resolve
Configure PyPI Trusted Publishing for the repo and cut the 0.4.2 tag to trigger the publish workflow
strengths: Apache-2.0 LICENSE in repo root; license = Apache-2.0 declared in pyproject
Clean src/ layout with hatchling build backend; three console scripts wired (jaxlint, jaxlint-lsp, jaxlint-mcp)
143 passed / 1 skipped locally with full extras; coverage 79.7% exceeds the 71% gate
PR CI runs merge-blocking jax-hlo job plus smoke/lsp/mcp markers — adequate signal for an alpha cut
LSP module shows 0% only because tests spawn a real server subprocess; integration tests pass and exercise the code
Documentation set is genuinely strong for a 0.4.x: roadmap, CLI, configuration, LSP, contributing, ADR 0001, rules reference
Development Status :: 3 - Alpha classifier honestly telegraphs API instability to consumers
Optional extras [docs|hlo|lsp|mcp] keep the base install lean and let users opt into heavy deps

summary: jaxlint 0.4.1 is alpha-ready: license, src layout, hatchling, 143 passing tests, 79.7% coverage, working CLI/LSP/MCP, and honest Alpha classifier — remaining gaps are pre-publish chicken-and-egg or post-ship polish.

blockers: No [project.urls] in pyproject.toml — PyPI page will have no Homepage/Source/Issues/Docs links
Classifiers omit 'Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11' and ':: 3.12' despite requires-python>=3.11 — PyPI search/filter discoverability and matrix advertised by CI is not declared in metadata

PyPI metadata authenticity: authors=[{name='Marielle'}] with no email; LICENSE Copyright says 'jaxlint contributors' (2026) — single-author project misrepresenting itself as a collective. Pick one and add a contact email (or org alias) before any first publish
PR CI runs only smoke/lsp/mcp markers; full ~100-test suite + coverage gate (fail_under=71) only on push to main. First external PR can land green while breaking unmarked tests — correctness risk

jaxlint.lsp.server shows 0% line coverage in parent process — language server entrypoint is effectively unverified end-to-end. 'works in subprocess tests' is not the same claim as 'jaxlint-lsp works after pip install'

No SECURITY.md, no CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, no top-level CONTRIBUTING.md (only docs/contributing.md), no SUPPORT/issue templates — required signals for a credible first public OSS release and supply-chain due diligence

No `python -m build` / sdist+wheel verification is documented or in CI. Hatchling defaults pack only [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages=['src/jaxlint']; sdist contents (tests/, docs/, LICENSE inclusion in wheel METADATA, py.typed) are unverified — risk of broken sdist install or missing license file in wheel

No clean-environment `pip install jaxlint==0.4.1` smoke test (twine check, install in fresh venv, run jaxlint --version, jaxlint-lsp --help, jaxlint-mcp --help) before publishing — the only thing standing between users and a yanked release
No git tags exist (`git tag -l` empty) and no documented tag/release cut process — PyPI Trusted Publishing flow needs a tag→workflow contract; releasing 0.4.1 from an untagged HEAD is unreproducible
Stale doc: docs/lsp.md still says 'as of 0.4.0' while pyproject is 0.4.1 — release-time doc audit checklist (which docs/index.md itself prescribes) has not been run
Canonical RTD/GitHub URLs in README and changelog still 404 (per orchestrator's own caveat) — README's first prominent link is broken at publish time
recommended_holds: HOLD publish until: (1) [project.urls] populated (Homepage, Source, Issues, Documentation, Changelog); (2) classifiers add Python 3.11 / 3.12 + 'Typing :: Typed' if py.typed lands; (3) author email + LICENSE copyright reconciled with single-author reality
HOLD until SECURITY.md + CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md + top-level CONTRIBUTING.md (or symlink to docs/contributing.md) + .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/* + PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md exist
HOLD until PR CI runs the full pytest suite + coverage gate on every PR (matrix already costs little; remove the 'main only' guard)

HOLD until LSP server in-process integration test exists (spawn jaxlint-lsp via subprocess+JSON-RPC, exchange initialize/didOpen/diagnostics, assert) and registers >0% coverage on jaxlint.lsp.server in the parent process (or document the subprocess-coverage approach explicitly)
HOLD until a release.yml workflow exists for PyPI Trusted Publishing, cut from an annotated git tag (v0.4.1), with `python -m build` + `twine check dist/*` + sdist install smoke in a clean container
HOLD until docs/lsp.md, README links, and the 'canonical hosted URLs' table all resolve (no 404s) — RTD project must be created and built once before publish, not after
HOLD on version number: either reset to 0.1.0 (matches Alpha) or graduate Dev Status to '4 - Beta'; do not ship 0.4.1 + Alpha
HOLD on OpenCode staging until jaxlint-mcp has been exercised via MCP Inspector and a transcript is attached to the release notes

RECOMMEND adding upper bound or 'tested with' note for jax in docs/install matrix, and a CI smoke job that does `pip install dist/jaxlint-0.4.1-*.whl` in a venv-from-scratch and runs `jaxlint --version`, `jaxlint-lsp --help`, `jaxlint-mcp --help`
risks: Semver / lifecycle mismatch: Development Status :: 3 - Alpha shipping at 0.4.1 with breaking changes between 0.x. Consumers reading 0.4.x assume mature pre-1.0 surface (à la ruff 0.x); reality is alpha. Either reset to 0.1.x or upgrade Dev Status to Beta — current combination is misleading
Supply-chain: no Trusted Publishing workflow committed (.github/workflows/release.yml absent). First publish via API token from a laptop is the highest-blast-radius path

No CHANGELOG release-notes section explicitly tagged for the 0.4.1 *release* (docs/changelog.md has 0.4.1 bullets but no date, no 'Unreleased' graduation, no link to the git tag/PyPI release that doesn't yet exist)
OpenCode staging is theoretical: the orchestrator has not (per the conclusion) actually run jaxlint-mcp through MCP Inspector or any real client — 'shippable to OpenCode' is an unsubstantiated claim
Copyright '2026' + a project with no public history may look like a typosquat / supply-chain seedling to scanners (Sigstore/OSV/socket.dev) — increases odds of being flagged on first publish

[project.optional-dependencies].docs pins exact versions (sphinx==8.2.3 etc.) — fine for RTD reproducibility but couples PyPI metadata to a frozen docs toolchain that downstreams may resolve unnecessarily; should at minimum be ~= bounds or a separate dependency-group
jax-hlo CI pins jax==0.10.0 / jaxlib==0.10.0 — reproducible but the published package advertises 'jax>=0.4.30' with no upper bound; users on jax 0.4.x get untested behaviour
No py.typed marker visible in src/jaxlint/ — claims of being a library (`jaxlint.core`, `jaxlint.hlo`) without typing distribution is a soft credibility hit
